title: Ekwo module manifest, version 1
description: What a module of Ekwo OS says about itself. One file, `modules/<code>/module.json`, read by `ekwo module list|enable|migrate`, by the MCP loader and by the guard tests. Everything a module *does* is in its migrations; this says where it lives and what it is allowed to reach.

code.description: The module's identifier, and the key of `public.modules`. Immutable once published: it is written on every entry the module posts.

schema.description: The Postgres schema the module lives in. One schema per module, never `public`, and PostgREST only serves it once it is listed in the project's exposed schemas.

version.description: Semver, on the same scale a pack uses: a label is a patch, a table or a column is a minor, a change that asks a company to do something is a major.

status.description: draft: installed and refused by enable_module(). available: enableable. deprecated: the companies that hold it keep working and no new one may enable it.

requires_socle_min.description: The oldest socle migration this module needs, by its timestamp version. `ekwo module enable` compares it against the migration history and refuses rather than letting a foreign key fail halfway.

posts.description: Whether this module writes to the ledger, always through post_module_entry(). A module that says false is held to it: a test refuses post_module_entry in its migrations.

prefix.description: Every MCP tool of this module is named `<prefix>_<verb>`, so a model reading a tool list can tell which module answers for what.

pack.description: The country data this module reads, if any. A module with no `pack` section has no country rule at all — which is most of them.

section.description: The file a country pack carries for this module: `packs/<cc>/<section>.json`, compiled by `ekwo pack build` into `supabase/seed/modules/<code>/`.
